Thought: Looking at the carbon NMR spectra, I can see several peaks in the aromatic region (typically 100-160 ppm):
- 138.76 ppm
- 131.45 ppm (appears twice)
- 130.59 ppm (appears twice)
- 121.30 ppm

The peaks at 43.47 and 38.60 ppm are clearly aliphatic carbons (not aromatic).

In the aromatic region, we have:
1. One carbon at 138.76 ppm
2. Two equivalent carbons at 131.45 ppm
3. Two equivalent carbons at 130.59 ppm
4. One carbon at 121.30 ppm

This gives us a total of 6 aromatic carbons.
